A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DLF, with readable main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices. Relocated and renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original compression evaluations, reconstructed images, component ablations and coding-time measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains the original compression evaluations, qualitative results, ablations and timing measurements.

M1.justification: The dual branches, interactive transforms, VQ/SQ quantization, latent adaptor and two-stage objectives remain unchanged. Naming the previously unspecified entropy model in v3 adds implementation documentation without establishing a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use Open Images training data and evaluate Kodak, CLIC2020, MS-COCO 30K and DIV2K. Full-resolution and cropped CLIC2020 evaluations already appear in v1; their redistribution between main text and appendix adds no coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged after matching corresponding experiments. The apparent replacement of TCM and HiFiC by PerCo and DiffEIC in Figure 9 reflects exchanging existing qualitative comparisons with the appendix, not adding or removing evaluated methods.

E3.justification: Training schedules, crop sizes, batch sizes, evaluation metrics and patch-based FID/KID procedures are retained. The training-schedule paragraph duplicated in v3 Appendix A.1 does not specify additional training.

E4.justification: Table 2 retains the same detail-branch, interaction and VQ-versus-SQ ablations. Entropy visualizations, complexity analysis and qualitative cases are also retained; enlarging and relocating an existing example adds no analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report identical mean and standard-deviation coding times in Table 3. No additional seed information, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests are introduced.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and the quantitative curves retain their results, including CLIC2020 BD-rates of -27.93% for LPIPS and -53.55% for DISTS. Qualitative scores also match: v1 Figure 9 becomes v3 Figure 20, while the final row of v1 Figure 20 becomes v3 Figure 9.

T1.justification: Equations 1–9 retain the same encoding, reconstruction and training-loss definitions. Neither version contains formal theorems or proofs, and v3 adds no mathematical derivation or assumption.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain semantic/detail decomposition, cross-branch redundancy reduction and strong perceptual compression at extremely low bitrates. The headline bitrate savings and fidelity, realism and decoding-speed claims are retained.

C2.justification: The explanations of adaptive detail allocation, redundancy reduction and generation-error correction remain substantively the same. The expanded correction explanation in v3 Section 3.2 already appears in v1 Section 2.2. The non-real-time coding limitation is unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 3.1 and Appendix A.1 newly identify and cite the quadtree-partition-based entropy/context model. The abstract replaces the future code-availability statement with a project link; the PDFs alone do not establish what resources that site provides.

R1.justification: v3 adds references concerning quadtree context models, EVC and newer diffusion codecs such as PICD and StableCodec. It also corrects tokenizer-method attributions in the introduction and Figure 3. The substantive positioning against HybridFlow and other codec families remains stable.

P1.justification: Local grammar corrections, clarified method explanations and a shortened qualitative-results discussion preserve the original narrative and section structure. Appendix A.1 introduces an editorial defect by repeating the entire training-schedule paragraph.

P2.justification: Existing qualitative comparisons are exchanged between the main text and appendix, with v1 Figure 9 enlarged into v3 Figure 20. Captions, bitrate-direction arrows and surrounding layout are adjusted. Architecture diagrams and quantitative plots remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Identifying the entropy estimator and correcting tokenizer attributions modestly improve implementation transparency and explanatory accuracy. Language cleanup and clearer qualitative displays also help, while the empirical evidence remains unchanged. The duplicated schedule paragraph in Appendix A.1 is a small editorial regression that limits, but does not outweigh, these gains.
